title: Maria the Virgin Witch
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: During the Hundred Years' War in France, the witch Maria uses summoned creatures, including a succubus and an incubus, to break up battles and protect villagers. The Archangel Michael orders her to stop and curses her to lose her powers if she loses her virginity; across three volumes she clashes with Heaven, other witches and some of the people she tries to save.
life_message: Refusing to accept war and suffering as the will of higher powers, and acting with compassion even at cost to oneself.

content.note: Medieval war backdrop; Maria's beasts frighten soldiers and Michael strikes her with a spear (publisher blurb, reviews).
Darker turns as Heaven and other witches oppose Maria (review of vol. 3).
Crude sex humor, a succubus seducing soldiers, an incubus, partial nudity; MU also lists attempted rape. Not explicit per ANN review.
Bawdy talk implied by reviews; profanity level not reported (to verify).
Medieval setting; nothing specific reported (to verify).
Defying authority for a cause is celebrated; little directly imitable.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Maria rejects the warriors' glory and honor culture; she wants fighting to stop.

Order vs freedom.evidence: Maria defies Heaven's order and other witches to follow her own conscience.

Civic vs kin.evidence: She protects the whole village and both armies' soldiers, not just kin.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Archangel Michael's rank is resisted; Maria questions divine and feudal hierarchy.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Theological debate where reason and compassion challenge received religious authority.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: War-torn survival setting, yet Maria prizes her own judgment and freedom.

folkways.japan: A Japanese seinen take on medieval European Christianity, using Western religious figures as story elements rather than from a believer's perspective.

delivery.evidence: Reviewers note 'philosophical and theological reflection' and talks on happiness and love described as 'a little forced'; ANN does not call it preachy.

personified.ideology: compassion and peace over divine order

delivery.note: Characters argue the theological questions openly, with Heaven's position given voice through a stern enforcer.

winners_losers: Maria keeps her ideals while learning the world is more complicated; the story sympathizes with her compassion over Heaven's rule (reviews).
